s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial papules with angiofibroma-like histology
salient_findings: Skin-colored, dome-shaped firm papules over the chin, nose, and perinasal region
Papules increased in size and number since age 18
Dozens of papules present on physical examination
Conical-shaped teeth
Dome-shaped lesion with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels on histology
key_facts: 28-year-old white man
Presented with skin-colored, dome-shaped firm papules
Papules located over the chin, nose, and perinasal region
Papules first noticed at age 18
Papules increased in size and number over time
History of right renal transplant at age 14
Physical examination revealed dozens of skin-colored dome-shaped papules
No hypopigmented macules, periungual fibromas, or Shagreen plaques present
Dental examination showed several teeth with a conical shape
Histologic analysis showed a dome-shaped lesion with plump fibroblasts and increased blood vessels
Electron microscopy showed dermal fibroblasts with prominent crystalline inclusions

shortlist.label: Tuberous Sclerosis Complex
shortlist.why_kept: Characteristic facial angiofibromas and history of renal transplant suggest possible TSC

shortlist.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple facial fibrofolliculomas and perifollicular fibromas are consistent with BHD

shortlist.label: Fibrofolliculoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic analysis showing angiofibroma-like features and presence of fibrofolliculomas

shortlist.label: Perifollicular Fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of skin-colored, dome-shaped papules and histologic findings

shortlist.label: Angiofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Histologic analysis showing characteristic features of angiofibroma

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple angiofibromas, particularly on the face, and a history of renal transplant suggesting possible renal angiomyolipoma, along with dental abnormalities such as conical teeth, are highly suggestive of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.

rejected.label: Birt-Hogg-Dube Syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic lung cysts, renal tumors, and fibrofolliculomas

rejected.label: Fibrofolliculoma
rejected.why: Not typically associated with the breadth of systemic findings or specific dental abnormalities seen in this patient

rejected.label: Perifollicular Fibroma
rejected.why: Does not account for the full spectrum of clinical findings, especially the renal transplant and dental anomalies

rejected.label: Angiofibroma
rejected.why: While histologically consistent, it does not explain the full clinical picture and systemic involvement
